learning_objectives.text: Name at least three evidence-based phishing indicators.
Choose an appropriate response: report, verify through a separate channel, or take no action.
Recognize that a legitimate message can look urgent, and that one indicator alone is not proof.

email.subject: URGENT: Password expires in 1 hour
email.body:
Hello,

Your Brightfield network password expires in 1 hour. To avoid losing access to your account, confirm your password now using the link below.

Confirm password: https://sso.brightfield.example/reset

IT Helpdesk

clues.explanation: The sender's domain is not the company's real domain (brightfield.example). The letter l has been swapped for the digit 1.
Urgent wording pressures you to act before you have time to check.
Asking you to enter your password through an emailed link is a common credential-theft pattern.
The text of the link shows one address, but the link actually goes to a different one. Check where a link really goes before you click.

action_feedback.report: Correct. Several independent clues point to phishing, and reporting lets the security team warn others.
action_feedback.verify_separately: A safe choice. Contacting IT through a channel you already know (not the email) confirms the message. Reporting it as well helps protect coworkers.
action_feedback.no_action: Not clicking protects you, but others may still receive this message. Reporting lets the security team act on it.

hints.basic: Look closely at the sender's domain and at where the link really goes.

ai.text: The sender's domain looks slightly different from the company's usual one. Check it carefully.

sources.title: Phishing Guidance: Stopping the Attack Cycle at Phase One

email.subject: Scheduled badge reader maintenance tonight
email.body:
Hi all,

The badge readers on floors 2 and 3 will be offline from 11 PM to 1 AM tonight for scheduled maintenance. Use the side entrance during this window.

No action is needed on your part. Questions? Reach the Facilities desk at the number on the intranet.

Facilities Team

clues.explanation: The sender's domain matches the company's real domain.
The message does not ask for a password, payment, or click.
It points you to a channel you already know instead of a link or phone number inside the email.
The message is time-sensitive, but it only gives information. It does not pressure you to act or hand over anything.

action_feedback.report: This message looks legitimate: the sender's domain matches and it asks for nothing. Reporting real messages creates extra work for the security team, though checking when unsure is a good habit.
action_feedback.verify_separately: Reasonable if you were unsure. Here the clues all point to a genuine notice, so no further action was needed.
action_feedback.no_action: Correct. The domain matches, nothing is requested, and it points to a known internal channel. Time-sensitive does not mean malicious.

hints.basic: Ask what the message wants you to do, and check whether the sender's domain matches the company's.

ai.text: Nothing here asks you to click or share information, though the timing is worth noting.

sources.title: Phishing Guidance: Stopping the Attack Cycle at Phase One
